injuries.longComment: Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.

injuries.shortComment: Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23, Week 10 win over Tennessee. He also returned five kickoffs for 142 yards.
injuries.longComment: Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.

injuries.shortComment: Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
injuries.longComment: The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

injuries.shortComment: Washington caught seven of nine targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
injuries.longComment: The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

injuries.shortComment: Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. He added 27 yards on four carries.
injuries.longComment: It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Giants.

injuries.shortComment: Strange caught two of three targets for nine yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
injuries.longComment: The Jaguars keep blowing out their opponents, and Strange contributed a three-yard touchdown Sunday but was otherwise not heard from much, as Parker Washington dog-walked the Titans' secondary for 7-152-1 receiving on nine targets. Strange's touchdown grab was his first since Week 1. He remans a locked-in TE1 for fantasy, as he is playing virtually every snap in an elite offense.

injuries.shortComment: The Chiefs elevated Carter from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Carter has been brought up from the practice squad for a second consecutive week to give the Chiefs more depth in the backfield in the absence of Kenneth Walker (groin). Carter operated as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson in Week 10 against the Falcons, but the former's role could be limited to special-teams duties since Jaydn Ott (hamstring) has been cleared to return from a one-game absence.

injuries.shortComment: Norman-Lott (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against Arizona.
injuries.longComment: Norman-Lott was removed from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he may not be ready to make his 2026 regular-season debut as he continues to work his way back from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. His return would give the Chiefs more depth on the interior defensive line behind starters Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga.

injuries.shortComment: Moore (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Moore will miss a second consecutive game due to an ankle injury, which means Joshua Ezeudu will likely start at right tackle against Arizona. Moore's next chance to play is Week 12 against Buffalo on Thanksgiving Day.

injuries.shortComment: Smith (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Smith entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons. He was unable to practice all week, and his absence means Mike Caliendo will likely start at right guard Sunday. Smith's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bills on Thanksgiving Day.

injuries.shortComment: Kelce (ankle/calf) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Kelce was forced from last Sunday's game against the Falcons with the ankle injury, but he's good to go for Week 11 against a hapless Arizona squad. The Chiefs should run all over the Cardinals defense and likely won't need much pass volume from Patrick Mahomes. Kelce is more of a fringe TE1 for fantasy purposes.

injuries.shortComment: With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Johnson is in line to handle workhorse duties for the second straight week, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: There was no sense in pushing Walker to play against a Cardinals team that is injury-ruined and likely to be blown out at Arrowhead. Johnson will get another crack at RB1 duties after he dismantled Atlanta's defense for 171 total yards and two touchdowns on 28 touches last Sunday. He's a top fantasy RB play.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Walker, who wasn't able to practice this week, will thus target a potential return Thursday against the Bills. The Chiefs -- per ESPN.com -- are "optimistic" he will play Thanksgiving night, but they will err on the side of caution with a short week ahead, and as such Emmett Johnson -- who rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10 -- is headed toward a second consecutive start this weekend.

injuries.shortComment: Bolton (shin) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Bolton popped up on the Chiefs' injury report with a shin issue Wednesday, but it doesn't look like it was anything serious. He's fifth in the league in total tackles (89) going into a Week 11 matchup versus a pass-happy Cardinals offense.

injuries.shortComment: The Chiefs placed Wiley (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

injuries.shortComment: Ott (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

injuries.shortComment: Tranquill recorded nine total tackles (six solo) during Sunday's 35-13 victory over the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: Tranquill finished tied for the team lead in tackles with fellow linebacker Nick Bolton in Week 10, notching at least nine takedowns for the third time in four weeks after not having reached that mark in any of the team's first five games of the year. On the season, Tranquill has now produced 75 total tackles (39 solo), two passes defensed and a fumble recovery over nine contests so far.

injuries.shortComment: Williams recorded five total tackles (two solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: Williams was able to register at least five takedowns for the third time this season, and his biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he intercepted a deep pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix. The interception was his second of the year, and he has now compiled 41 total tackles (23 solo) and 11 passes defensed over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Briningstool caught one of two targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win against the Jets on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Briningstool connected with Patrick Mahomes for a 20-yard reception midway through the first quarter but didn't record another reception. The 23-year-old tight end has exactly one catch in each of his past three games. That's not enough production to warrant fantasy consideration, but Briningstool is at least showing growth as a pass catcher, as he had just one catch on two targets over his first six contests of the campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Butker made all five PATs in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Butker did not attempt a field goal in the contest, as the Chiefs solely scored touchdowns. He now moves to 27-for-28 on PATs in 2026 as he continues to struggle to hold onto the starting kicker job.

injuries.shortComment: Gray caught one of three targets for six yards during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: Gray was unable to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after he had at least two catches in each of the team's previous five games prior to Week 9. The tight end did play a season-high 53 offensive snaps with Travis Kelce being limited to just 18 snaps on offense as a result of an ankle injury. If Kelce is forced to be limited or even miss the team's Week 11 matchup with Arizona, Gray would stand to operate as the team's primary tight end in his place.

injuries.shortComment: Armstrong caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

injuries.shortComment: Allen caught two of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

injuries.shortComment: Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injuries.longComment: Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

injuries.shortComment: Downs secured four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled once but recovered and returned three punts for 10 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Making his Chiefs debut following three days of practice after arriving via trade from the Colts on Tuesday, Downs looked right at home in the Patrick Mahomes-led offense. The young wideout fully capitalized on the upgrade he saw at quarterback, finishing third in receptions, receiving yards and targets right out of the gate and adding his second touchdown of the season on a difficult 18-yard catch just before halftime. Downs' immediate chemistry with Mahomes is highly welcome news for fantasy managers, and he'll aim to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Rice brought in five of six targets for 82 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Rice led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in receptions and targets on a prolific afternoon for the Chiefs' air attack. Rice didn't get in on the scoring fun of a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes, but he still eclipsed 80 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 3. Rice's level of involvement was encouraging given the debuting Josh Downs drew five targets, keeping the former's prospects bright for a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 15 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Taking advantage of a controlled environment and a fast track at Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- not to mention the presence of the debuting Josh Downs -- Mahomes repeatedly exploited the vulnerabilities of the Falcons defense throughout the afternoon. The legendary signal-caller showed no ill effects from the elbow injury that he'd suffered in Week 9, and he connected with Emmett Johnson (12, six yards), Downs (18 yards), Cyrus Allen (39 yards) and Andrew Armstrong (43 yards) for his quintet of touchdown passes. Mahomes now has multiple scoring strikes and zero interceptions in three straight games, and Sunday's five TD tosses represented a new season high. Mahomes will take 2,385 passing yards and a 19:4 TD:INT into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: The Raiders elevated Runyon from the practice squad Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Las Vegas is bringing up Runyon with Brock Bowers (ankle) listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos. Runyon appeared in 13 games with the Raiders last season but logged just 45 offensive snaps and caught only one pass for three yards. He's depth behind Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas.

injuries.shortComment: Fatukasi (toe) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Paul Gutierrez of the Raiders' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Fatukasi was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice before downgrading to a DNP on Thursday. The defensive lineman capped off Week 11 prep with a full session Friday but remains questionable for Sunday's divisional bout. If Fatukasi cannot suit up, the absence of Tonka Hemingway (stinger) means Thomas Booker and Tim Keenan will likely start alongside nose tackle Adam Butler for Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Hemingway (upper body) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Broncos, Paul Gutierrez of the Raiders' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Hemingway did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions as he continues to deal with a stinger injury he likely suffered in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. With Hemingway ruled out and Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) listed as questionable, Thomas Booker is currently the only healthy defensive end for the Raiders as they head into a divisional bout.

injuries.shortComment: Coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that Bowers (ankle) is slated to be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Bowers, who was limited at Thursday's practice, was back on the field Friday, but the tight end nonetheless will head into the weekend with a questionable designation. Look for added intel regarding his Week 11 status to arrive late Saturday or early Sunday via the usual assortment of NFL insiders, but if Bowers is limited or ends up out for his team's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, fellow TE Michael Mayer will merit fantasy lineup consideration while facing 7-2 Denver.

injuries.shortComment: Gay (hip) was spotted at practice Friday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Gay, who was limited Wednesday, logged a DNP on Thursday, but it looks like he'll work in some capacity to close out the week. Per Warren, the Raiders worked out three kickers with Gay injured, but it appears as though it's only Gay and practice-squad member Kansei Matsuzawa available to handle kicks at Friday's practice.

injuries.shortComment: Booker (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: An ankle injury has sidelined Booker for each of the Raiders' last two games. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that he's recovered from his injury and on track to play in Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Broncos. Booker has accumulated 13 tackles (nine solo) across seven regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Paye (neck) was not listed on the Raiders' injury report Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Paye made an early exit in the second half of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with a neck injury. The linebacker did not return to the contest, but the issue does not seem to have been serious. Paye is healthy and appears ready to log consistent full practices throughout Week 11 prep.

injuries.shortComment: Thornton (back) was a full participant in Las Vegas' practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Thornton is healthy again after sitting out the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to a back injury. However, it is still unlikely that the 23-year-old plays in Sunday's matchup versus the Broncos, as Thornton had been a healthy scratch every week since returning from injured reserve in late October prior to Week 10.

injuries.shortComment: Chinn tallied seven tackles (three solo) in a loss to Seattle on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Chinn continues to put up consistent tackling numbers, as he's now logged at least seven stops in six straight games. The veteran safety has played all but one of Las Vegas' defensive snaps this season. He's up to 72 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two recovered fumbles through 10 contests.

injuries.shortComment: Walker posted eight tackles (four solo) and recovered a fumble against Seattle in Sunday's Week 10 loss.
injuries.longComment: Walker, Nakobe Dean and Maxx Crosby all had eight tackles Sunday to co-lead the team. Walker added a fumble recovery on the second play of the game that helped set up a Raiders touchdown. The veteran linebacker has remained productive in his first season with Las Vegas following four years in Green Bay. Walker has 80 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, and two recovered fumbles though 10 contests on the campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Dean registered eight tackles (five solo) and recovered a fumble Sunday in a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Dean tied for the team lead in stops with Maxx Crosby and Quay Walker. Nonetheless, the veteran linebacker saw his five-game streak of double-digit tackles come to an end. Dean did contribute his first recovered fumble of the season when he scooped up a ball that was turned over by Seattle QB Drew Lock in the fourth quarter. Dean is tied with Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton for the NFL lead with 107 tackles, though Denver has played one fewer game.

injuries.shortComment: Crosby finished Sunday's loss to Seattle with eight tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks.
injuries.longComment: Crosby tied for the team lead with his season-high eight stops. Among those tackles, four went for a loss, including a fourth-quarter sack of Drew Lock. After registering just a half-sack over six games from Week 2 to Week 7, Crosby has since finished with exactly 1.0 sacks in each of his past three contests. He's at 5.0 sacks overall through 10 games as he seeks a fifth NFL campaign with double-digit sacks.

injuries.shortComment: Bech caught two of seven targets for 10 yards during the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

injuries.shortComment: Young went without a target while playing one of the Raiders' 59 snaps on offense in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. He also brought back one kickoff for 29 yards.
injuries.longComment: Young has suited up in each of the Raiders' 10 games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams. He's seen single-digit snaps on offense in five straight games and has posted a collective 2-36-0 receiving line on three targets on the campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Nailor recorded one reception for minus-1 yard on four targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.

injuries.shortComment: Laube played all 22 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and returned two kickoffs for 46 yards and one punt for zero yards.
injuries.longComment: Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

injuries.shortComment: Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

injuries.shortComment: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

injuries.shortComment: Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 22 yards and one TD during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.

injuries.shortComment: Washington compiled eight rushes for 23 yards and secured his only target for four yards during Sunday's 21-13 defeat to the Seahawks.
injuries.longComment: Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has logged 54 rushes along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.

injuries.shortComment: The Chargers placed Shelley (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Shelley was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets due to an ankle injury. His placement on IR means he must miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the 49ers on Thursday, Dec. 17. Shelley has contributed both on defense and special teams and has eight solo tackles and a pass defense across six regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: The Chargers activated Pipkins (knee) from injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Pipkins is still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets, but his activation from injured reserve is a good sign for his availability. If he's cleared to play, then he would likely reclaim his starting role at left guard. Pipkins landed on IR in mid-September due to a knee injury.

injuries.shortComment: Dupree requested his release from the Chargers earlier this week, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Dupree also asked for a trade earlier in the season, but the Chargers have so far not granted his request. The veteran edge rusher has been limited to special teams over the Chargers' last two games and has yet to record a sack. If he's let go by the Chargers, then Dupree could garner interest from teams looking for a boost in the pass rush.

injuries.shortComment: Waxter (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Waxter ended Week 11 prep with consecutive limited sessions after being a non-participant Wednesday. If Waxter cannot suit up for Sunday's game, Deane Leonard is set to be the only reserve cornerback behind starters Cam Hart, Donte Jackson and Tarheeb Still (ankle).

injuries.shortComment: Williamson (calf) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Williamson ended Week 11 prep with consecutive DNPs. The strong safety remains sidelined with a calf injury he sustained in Week 8 against the Rams.

injuries.shortComment: Eboigbe (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Eboigbe was unable to play against the Ravens this past Monday due to an ankle injury. He ended Week 11 prep with a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. His return means there will be less rotational snaps at defensive end for rookie fifth-rounder Nick Barrett.

injuries.shortComment: Still (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Still was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to an ankle injury. His late addition to the injury report isn't a great sign ahead of Sunday's game, and if he's unable to play, then Deane Leonard and Genesis Smith would both be in line for more snaps in the Chargers' secondary.

injuries.shortComment: Henley (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Henley was unable to practice all week, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said Friday that the fourth-year linebacker has been working through knee soreness since Monday's win against the Ravens, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Denzel Perryman and Marlowe Wax figure to be the top candidates to start at inside linebacker alongside Del'Shawn Phillips in the absence of Henley, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.shortComment: Thompson (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Thompson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury and has not seen regular-season action since Week 2 against the Raiders. If he's ruled out for Sunday's game, then the rookie fourth-rounder's next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.shortComment: Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel told reporters Friday that his "expectation" is that Hampton is the lead back for the Chargers, Omar Navarro of the team's official site reports.
injuries.longComment: "Generally, my expecation is [Hampton] is our leading ball carrier every week.  ... I knew based on his last two practice weeks, we were feeling like he was going to have a breakout performance at any given time," McDaniel said Friday. That breakout game took place Monday against the Ravens, when Hampton turned 22 carries into a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown in a 23-20 win for the Chargers. With the Chargers getting extra time to rest, Hampton's stock is trending up heading into Week 12 against the Jets, whose defense ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3) and 29th in rushing touchdowns allowed (13).

injuries.shortComment: Kolar (concussion) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: The tight end is still in the concussion protocol, so he'll be up against it to clear the final hurdles, especially after the Chargers played Monday night against Baltimore. If Kolar is ruled out, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden should handle most of the tight-end duties for the Bolts.

injuries.shortComment: McConkey (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: McConkey, who didn't record any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms and was inactive in Week 10, has been able to practice in a limited fashion thus far this week, but thanks to his official 'questionable' designation, his status will need to be tracked in advance of Sunday's 4:05 ET kickoff. If McConkey is limited or out versus New York, Tre' Harris could maintain a key role in the Chargers' pass-catching corps alongside fellow WR Quentin Johnston.

injuries.shortComment: Tomlinson recorded five tackles (three solo) including 2.0 sacks during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
injuries.longComment: In a game where Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett dropped back 51 times, there were no shortage of opportunities for the Chargers to rush the passer, and Tomlinson came away with the best single-game sack total of his nine-plus year career so far. He has taken on a larger role on the defensive line than 2025 third-rounder Jamaree Caldwell in recent weeks, and only Teair Tart played as many snaps on the Chargers' defensive front as Tomlinson did (36) in Week 10.

injuries.shortComment: Phillips recorded nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
injuries.longComment: Phillips was in the right place at the right time when a Jacoby Brissett pass bounced off the helmet of rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane in the second quarter, and the turnover set up a Chargers touchdown that put the team ahead 17-7. His tackle total was also his highest going back to Week 18 of the 2023 season with the Ravens. With that said, his role in the Chargers' defense is still not big enough to warrant IDP consideration in most formats.

injuries.shortComment: Dicker made all three of his field-goal tries and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
injuries.longComment: Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

injuries.shortComment: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Njoku's snap count was predictably capped as he returned from a six-game absence due to a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. With another week under his belt to get back up to speed, Njoku could be more involved in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore.
injuries.longComment: Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
injuries.longComment: Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (one), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell appear to be falling into rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
injuries.longComment: One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

injuries.shortComment: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
injuries.longComment: Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers' air attack something to hang its collective hat on heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Awosika (fibula) is active for Monday's game against the Ravens.
injuries.longComment: Awosika will suit up Monday for the first time since Week 2, when he suffered an injury to his fibula. He should slide back into his starting role at left guard.

injuries.shortComment: Taylor (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Monday.
injuries.longComment: Taylor is battling an ankle injury and was ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with Baltimore. Now on injured reserve, he will be required to miss at least four games before being eligible to return.

injuries.shortComment: Nacua (knee) is expected to be sidelined 4-to-5 months after undergoing MCL surgery, which means he likely won't be able to return to action even if the Rams advance to the Super Bowl, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: This update provides a firmer timeline than prior reports and confirms Nacua won't be available for the remainder of the regular season or the playoffs. The Rams have already placed him on injured reserve and will look to others to help fill the massive void in the WR corps left by Nacua's injury. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on IR and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers.

injuries.shortComment: Coach Sean McVay said Saturday that Avila (hamstring) will not play in Wednesday's game against the Packers, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
injuries.longComment: The Rams' left guard was injured in Week 9 against the Commanders and will miss a second straight game. Bill Murray or Justin Dedich (undisclosed) projects to start in Avila's place versus Green Bay.

injuries.shortComment: The Rams opened the 21-day practice window for Dedich (undisclosed) on Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Dedich opened the regular season on injured reserve due to an undisclosed injury. He's now been cleared to practice, and his participation over the next few days will factor into whether he's activated from IR ahead of Wednesday's game against Green Bay.

injuries.shortComment: The Rams designated Turner (groin) to return from injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Turner has missed the Rams' last four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Cardinals. His practice participation over the coming days will ultimately determine whether he'll be activated from IR ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Sean McVay said Saturday that Williams is tending to a sore toe but is expected to play Wednesday against the Packers, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: The Rams are in the midst of their Week 11 bye, but with a Wednesday game on tap in Week 12, the team is getting back on the practice field this weekend. He'll have three more days to work through the new health concern, but considering McVay's comments, Williams should be fine to continue to work in tandem with fellow RB Blake Corum.

injuries.shortComment: The Rams are expected to lean more on Mumpfield and the rest of the team's wide receivers in the absence of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), the latter of whom is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, Nate Atkins and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic report.
injuries.longComment: Nacua is expected to miss "a couple of months" after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his MCL, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. With Nacua and Davante Adams (hamstring, IR) sidelined for Week 10 against the Cardinals, Mumpfield operated as the Rams' WR1 for that contest and finished with three catches (on four targets) for 81 yards in a 34-6 win for Los Angeles. The Rams are "hopeful" that Adams will return soon, but if he's not activated from injured reserve ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers, then Mumpfield would lead Los Angeles' wide receiver group that also includes Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

injuries.shortComment: Coach Sean McVay noted Friday that Adams (hamstring) isn't expected to practice this weekend, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
injuries.longComment: Regarding the looming practice status of Adams, who is on IR and last played in Week 6, McVay said Friday, "We're not quite there yet." On the plus side, Beacham relays that the Rams still are hopeful Adams will be ready retake the field next week. The veteran pass-catcher's availability gains added import going forward, following Friday's report from Beacham that fellow starting WR Puka Nacua is on track to miss a couple of months after undergoing an MCL procedure.

injuries.shortComment: Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) isn't ready to return to game action, but the Rams still plan to activate him from injured reserve before Week 12 and keep him on the active roster, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
injuries.longComment: Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation at least would keep him off season-ending IR, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Adams (hamstring) are needed badly in this offense.

injuries.shortComment: Garrett played 17 defensive snaps but did not show up on the box score otherwise during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals in Week 10.
injuries.longComment: Garrett was cleared to play in Week 10 after working through a knee injury. The low snap count was more due to the fact that the Cardinals posted only 35 offensive snaps while recording a 17:37 time of possession. The Rams are on a bye for Week 11, so Garrett's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Lake posted two tackles (one solo) during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals in Week 10.
injuries.longComment: Lake recorded at least six tackles in each of the first nine games of the regular season, but he had only two stops in Week 10 despite playing every defensive snap. The fifth-year defensive back is up to 65 tackles (38 solo), 11 pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through 10 regular-season games heading into the Week 11 bye.

injuries.shortComment: Klare went without a target while playing four of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Klare has been a healthy inactive on three occasions this season, but he's now suited up in three straight games while the Rams have been short on pass-catching options due to injuries to tight end Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) and wideouts Puka Nacua (knee), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back). Despite those personnel losses, Klare has still struggled to carve out meaningful playing time, as fellow tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are all regarded as superior blockers and have been prioritized ahead of him. The rookie second-round pick out of Ohio State still has yet to draw a target through his first seven NFL games.

injuries.shortComment: out
injuries.longComment: out

injuries.shortComment: Daniels caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive, Daniels' 46 snaps were two fewer than Konata Mumpfield for the team lead at receiver for the Rams. Mumpfield led the group in targets (four), catches (three) and yards (81), and only Xavier Smith (2-40-1) joined him as wide receivers to catch more than one pass from Matthew Stafford against Arizona while the Rams relied heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Daniels' playing time isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

injuries.shortComment: Atwell caught one of two targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Despite both Puka Nacua (toe/knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being sidelined, Atwell still played just 16 of 76 offensive snaps versus Arizona and ran 15 routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks. Atwell played behind both Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at receiver for Los Angeles.

injuries.shortComment: Rivers rushed 15 times for 81 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

injuries.shortComment: Allen caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown in Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
injuries.longComment: With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

injuries.shortComment: McManus made both of his field-goal attempts and all four PATs in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: McManus' Sunday performance extends his perfect streak with a Rams' special teams unit that desperately needed consistency at kicker. He's now 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-14 on PATs after five regular-season contests as a Ram in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

injuries.shortComment: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Shelton (hamstring) is set to miss several weeks due to injury, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
injuries.longComment: The starting center is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury. Shelton will likely be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. Dylan McMahon (knee, IR) also sustained an injury in the Rams' Week 10 win over the Cardinals, leaving Beaux Limmer to finish out the contest at center and to likely fill in as the starter for the foreseeable future.

injuries.shortComment: The Rams placed McMahon (knee) on injured reserve Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
injuries.longComment: McMahon suffered a knee injury during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. The injury is severe enough for McMahon to require a stint on IR, so he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, with his next chance to play being Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas Day. With Coleman Shelton nursing a hamstring injury, the Rams may have to turn to other options like David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to fill in at center for the time being.

injuries.shortComment: The Dolphins activated Baker (knee) from the reserve/PUP list Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Baker opened the season on the Dolphins' PUP list due to a knee injury. He was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, and while he's still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills, Baker appears to be in line to make his 2026 regular-season debut. He played in all 17 regular-season games for the Titans in 2025 and finished with 55 tackles (39 solo) and seven pass defenses.

injuries.shortComment: The Dolphins elevated Carlson from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Carlson signed to the Dolphins' practice squad Tuesday, two weeks after being released by the Saints. Following the Dolphins' release of Zane Gonzalez, Carlson will operate as Miami's kicker for Sunday's game against Buffalo. In seven appearances with the Saints this season, Carlson went 8-for-12 on field-goal attempts (including 3-for-7 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 16-for-18 on extra-point tries.

injuries.shortComment: Simpson (knee) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Simpson upgraded to a limited participant in Friday's practice after missing consecutive sessions to start Week 11 prep. The reserve cornerback remains unlikely to suit up, but Friday's partial session gives the 26-year-old a chance to be active on game day.

injuries.shortComment: Pinion (groin) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Pinion did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions. The punter likely sustained his groin injury in the Dolphins' Week 10 loss to the Colts. Jack Browning is set to be elevated from the practice squad ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills to take over punting duties.

injuries.shortComment: Meyer (neck) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Meyer suffered a stinger against the Colts in Week 10, but his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's AFC East game. He would likely start at center for a second consecutive week if Aaron Brewer (concussion) is not cleared to play.

injuries.shortComment: Brewer (concussion) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Brewer was unable to play against the Colts in Week 10 while in the league's concussion protocol. He logged a full practice Friday, but he won't be allowed to suit up Sunday unless he passes an evaluation by an independent neurologist, which would get him out of protocol. Andrew Meyer would likely start at center if Brewer is not available.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Brents (neck) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Brents' practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday due to a neck injury, but his full session Friday was enough for the fourth-year defensive back to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt. Brents has accumulated 33 tackles (18 solo), one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Wayne (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Wayne will miss a second straight game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29. In his absence, Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will serve as the Dolphins' rotational wide receivers behind Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell.

injuries.shortComment: Bell (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Bills.
injuries.longComment: The rookie wideout is averaging 1.5 catches for 18.5 yards per game this season and is not in the conversation to start for fantasy teams with both Caleb Douglas and Malik Washington healthy.

injuries.shortComment: Douglas (shoulder) will play Sunday against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Douglas was managed during the practice week, but he's good to go for his normal every-down role Sunday against Buffalo. With the Dolphins installed as 16.5-point underdogs, Miami is projected to throw a ton in comeback mode. However, Douglas is a tough click for fantasy with Kyle McCord under center.

injuries.shortComment: Trader (shoulder/groin) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Bills, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
injuries.longComment: Trader opened the week as a non-participant in practice after suffering groin and shoulder injuries during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts last Sunday. Kyle Louis and Julius Wood may see more time in his place if Trader does indeed miss Week 11. Trader has 45 tackles (23 solo) and three pass breakups, including one interception, through nine 2026 regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Phillips underwent surgery on his injured bicep Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Phillips was recently placed on injured reserve with a season-ending biceps injury sustained in Week 10 versus the Colts. The 22-year-old ends his season with 28 tackles (11 solo) through nine games. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper are top candidates to see more reps at defensive tackle as the season continues.

injuries.shortComment: Brooks produced nine total tackles (six solo), a pass defensed and a forced fumble during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Brooks was able to register at least nine takedowns for the fourth straight game and seventh time overall this season. The linebacker was also able to strip Colts running back Jonathan Taylor in the first quarter, but offensive lineman Dalton Tucker was able to jump on the loose ball. Brooks is now up to 84 total tackles (38 solo) while also adding two passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine contests to open the 2026 season.

injuries.shortComment: Rodriguez recorded one solo tackle during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Rodriguez finished with fewer than eight takedowns for just the third time this season, and his one tackle was a season low for the rookie. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (36 solo), including a 1.0 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over nine contests so far during his rookie campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Taaffe recorded six total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Taaffe was able to register at least six stops for the third straight game and sixth time overall this season. The safety's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, securing his third interception of the year. On the year, Taaffe has compiled 53 total tackles (27 solo), three interceptions and a forced fumble over nine contests so far.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson recorded four total tackles (three solo) and a pick-six in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
injuries.longComment: Johnson was able to secure an interception for the second straight week, jumping in front of a pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in the third quarter, ultimately returning the interception for a 59-yard touchdown. The cornerback has now registered 46 total tackles (24 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine games this season.

injuries.shortComment: Coleman logged one catch for six yards on six targets in Sunday's Week 10 loss to Indianapolis.
injuries.longComment: Coleman couldn't get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL regular-season appearance. In fact, Coleman has been quiet inefficient regardless of who has thrown him the ball this year, as he has just nine receptions on 27 targets through nine games. Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.

injuries.shortComment: Cook was signed to the Dolphins' active roster Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Cook served as the team's No. 2 option at quarterback behind Kyle McCord in the team's 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, with Malik Willis (abdomen) being placed on injured reserve prior to the contest. Cook reverted to the practice squad Monday, but he has now officially become a member of the team's active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

injuries.shortComment: Biggers (knee) was placed on injured reserve by the Dolphins on Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Biggers suffered a lateral meniscus tear in Week 10, and he will now miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign while on IR. Fellow defensive lineman Jordan Phillips (biceps) was also placed on IR on Tuesday, and as a result, Kenneth Grant will operate as the team's top dog at defensive tackle moving forward this season.

injuries.shortComment: Wright turned three carries into minus-2 yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

injuries.shortComment: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-4 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

injuries.shortComment: Bartholomew should revert to a backup role with T.J. Hockenson returning from a wrist injury for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Bartholomew was targeted four times in Week 10 for three catches, 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end received more than one target in only one other game this season, Week 5, when Hockenson went down after two offensive snaps. While Bartholomew has proven himself a red-zone threat, Hockenson should return to seeing most of the tight end volume in Sunday's contest.

injuries.shortComment: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
injuries.longComment: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

injuries.shortComment: Rodgers (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
injuries.longComment: Rodgers popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a quad injury. His practice reps were also limited in Friday's session, and his status for Sunday's contest may not be officially known until the Vikings announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. Rookie fifth-rounder Charles Demmings and Zemaiah Vaughn would likely be the top candidates to start opposite James Pierre if Rodgers is not cleared to play against San Francisco.

injuries.shortComment: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
injuries.longComment: Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. He was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

injuries.shortComment: Cashman (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
injuries.longComment: Cashman will end up missing one game (Week 10 against the Packers) while in the league's concussion protocol, and his return means Ivan Pace will revert to a rotational role at inside linebacker for Sunday's contest. Cashman has accumulated 76 tackles (41 solo), including a career-high-tying 4.5 sacks, seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery across eight regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Murray (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: The quarterback lost his job to Kirk Cousins and will continue to manage a hamstring injury. Murray's availability will only matter moving forward if something happens to Cousins, either performance or injury related. Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer remain on the 53-man roster as backup options.

injuries.shortComment: Hockenson (wrist) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: After sitting out last Sunday against Green Bay and then logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Hockenson is ready to return against San Francisco in a potential playoff preview. His lack of a designation puts Minnesota's top tight end in position to reclaim his usual role in the passing game that now has Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Hockenson is a TE1 for fantasy purposes.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10.
injuries.longComment: The Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times in Week 10, with Wilson taking down the Packers quarterback for a six-yard loss early in the second quarter. Wilson has logged at least 0.5 sacks in three of his last four outings, and the veteran linebacker is up to 57 tackles (30 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense through nine regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: The Vikings placed Richter (foot) on injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

injuries.shortComment: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that Addison underwent thumb surgery earlier this week and won't be placed on injured reserve, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Thus, the Vikings are expecting Addison to recover fully before the four games required of an IR stint, but in any case he will miss some time due to the thumb injury he suffered in practice last Friday and sidelined him this past Sunday at Green Bay. With Addison out of the lineup, Minnesota will be relying on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price, Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver.

injuries.shortComment: Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: All three of Reichard's field goals came from fewer than 40 yards out in the contest. The return of Kirk Cousins allowed Minnesota's offense to surge to its highest touchdown total since Week 1, the team's first bout against the Packers. Reichard is now 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and remains perfect at 13-for-13 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.

injuries.shortComment: Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
injuries.longComment: Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
injuries.longComment: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.
injuries.longComment: Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.

injuries.shortComment: Jefferson caught nine of 13 targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
injuries.longComment: In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. The nine grabs and 13 targets were season highs for Jefferson, while the yardage total was his best showing since Week 5. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Metellus (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
injuries.longComment: Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
injuries.longComment: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

injuries.shortComment: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.
injuries.longComment: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that DeVito will start in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29, Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter of ESPN report.
injuries.longComment: Drake Maye was diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, which he sustained in the first quarter of the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich. DeVito filled in for the rest of that contest and completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning four carries into 19 yards. It appears he will be New England's starter coming out of the bye, with rookie seventh-rounder Behren Morton operating as the backup. However, there's been speculation that the Patriots could consider Daniel Jones, who was released by the Colts on Friday, as another option. Jones is available on waivers until 4:00 p.m. ET on Monday, after which the veteran signal caller would be a free agent if he goes unclaimed.

injuries.shortComment: Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: New England's trade for Brown is going down as one the team would definitely prefer to reverse. He's shown no chemistry with Drake Maye (ankle) and hasn't looked healthy since injuring his ankle in the first half of the Week 1 game against the Seahawks. Brown also appears to have lost multiple steps with his downfield speed due to the laundry list of lower-body injuries that now includes ankle, knee and hamstring issues in 2026. The Patriots will play out the string on a lost season without Maye and Brown for several more weeks. Look for Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) when healthy, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism to pick up the slack at wideout with Brown on the shelf again.

injuries.shortComment: Maye has suffered a fractured right fibula that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him for some time, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: Maye was knocked out of Week 10 action on the first possession of this past Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich. He already was expected to miss multiple games as a result of the injury, but with a diagnosis now available, he's now in rehab mode until further notice. A return at some point down the stretch likely will depend on the Patriots remaining in the playoff race, but for the time being Tommy DeVito will be under center in place of Maye.

injuries.shortComment: Elliss logged 10 tackles (three solo) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
injuries.longComment: Week 10 was the third time this season that Elliss posted double-digit stops, and he ended up co-leading the Patriots in tackles with safety Kevin Byard. Through 10 regular-season games, Elliss has accumulated 75 tackles (37 solo), including 1.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Elliss's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

injuries.shortComment: Byard registered 10 tackles (three solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
injuries.longComment: Byard picked off a Jared Goff pass intended for Jameson Williams in the end zone late in the second quarter, which halted the Lions' red zone drive in its tracks. It was the first time this season that Byard posted double-digit stops, and each of the veteran safety's two interceptions on the year have come over his last three outings. He enters the Week 11 bye with 53 tackles (26 solo) and five pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
injuries.longComment: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests.
